**4B.6 Research Note: Bola Ahmed Tinubu (2024)**

Bottom line: **mostly negative**. I found **some general pro-democracy rhetoric** and a few mixed statements about dialogue, but the strongest 2024 evidence points the other way: **journalists were charged, cybercrime law was used against critical reporting, and public-order enforcement chilled protest and scrutiny**. I found **no strong direct evidence** that Tinubu actively protected independent media or expanded information access.

- [President Tinubu Receives U.S. Ambassador, underscores importance of sustaining democracy, its norms and institutions](https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-receives-u-s-ambassador-underscores-importance-of-sustaining-democracy-its-norms-and-institutions/) | State House | 2024-07-25  
  Tinubu said protests are part of democracy and drew a line only against destruction of lives and property. This is the clearest pro-democratic public statement I found, but it is general rhetoric, not a concrete protection for media independence or information access.  
  Question IDs: `4B.6`, also `4B.3`

- [President Tinubu’s Broadcast on the Nationwide Protest](https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubus-broadcast-on-the-nationwide-protest/) | State House | 2024-08-04  
  Tinubu acknowledged legitimate hopes among protesters, addressed the public directly, and asked for a pause for dialogue while telling law enforcement to protect lives and property. This is mildly positive for open communication, but it does not show protection of journalists or anti-censorship restraint.  
  Question IDs: `4B.6`, also `4B.3`, `3B.8`, `3B.9`

- [Nigeria security forces deploy, government offers dialogue as protests loom](https://www.investing.com/news/economic-indicators/nigeria-security-forces-deploy-government-offers-dialogue-as-protests-loom-3546462) | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-07-31  
  Reuters reported that the government offered dialogue while security forces deployed in major cities. This is mixed evidence: the dialogue offer is a restraint signal, but the coercive posture undercuts a clean reading of information openness.  
  Question IDs: `4B.6`, also `3B.8`, `3B.9`

- [Nigeria: Government Warnings Raise Concerns about Upcoming Protests](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/07/29/nigerian-government-warnings-raise-concerns-about-upcoming-protests) | Human Rights Watch | 2024-07-29  
  HRW said senior officials and security agencies were already framing the planned protests as regime-change activity and warning of chaos and violence. That is negative evidence because it shows a fear-based state narrative rather than protection of open information and dissent.  
  Question IDs: `4B.6`, also `3B.8`, `3B.9`

- [Nigeria: Police used excessive force to violently quash #EndBadGovernance protests](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/11/nigeria-police-used-excessive-force-to-violently-quash-endbadgovernance-protests/) | Amnesty International | 2024-11-28  
  Amnesty documented killings, mass detentions, and torture during the August crackdown, and said authorities denied wrongdoing. This is strong negative evidence for information access because coercive policing tends to chill reporting, monitoring, and public scrutiny.  
  Question IDs: `4B.6`, also `3B.8`, `3B.9`, `3B.10`

- [Nigeria police charge 4 journalists with cybercrimes for corruption reporting](https://cpj.org/2024/10/nigeria-police-charge-4-journalists-with-cybercrimes-for-corruption-reporting/) | Committee to Protect Journalists | 2024-10-03  
  CPJ said four journalists were charged under the Cybercrimes Act despite February reforms. This is direct negative evidence: legal pressure on journalists is the opposite of protecting independent media and information access.  
  Question IDs: `4B.6`, also `4B.3`, `4B.4`, `4B.5`

- [4 Nigerian journalists charged with cybercrime, defamation over fraud investigation](https://cpj.org/2024/02/4-nigerian-journalists-charged-with-cybercrime-defamation-over-fraud-investigation/) | Committee to Protect Journalists | 2024-02-09  
  Police arrested and charged journalists over reporting on alleged corruption at a state polytechnic. This is another concrete example of press intimidation rather than tolerance of investigative reporting.  
  Question IDs: `4B.6`, also `4B.3`, `4B.4`, `4B.5`

- [Nigeria: Freedom on the Net 2024](https://freedomhouse.org/country/nigeria/freedom-net/2024) | Freedom House | 2024  
  Freedom House said the Cybercrimes Act’s cyberstalking provision had frequently been used against journalists and activists, contributing to takedowns and self-censorship. This is the clearest broad negative signal that independent media and information access remained vulnerable.  
  Question IDs: `4B.6`, also `4B.2`, `4B.3`, `4B.4`, `4B.5`

- [Nigeria charges protesters with treason, inciting military](https://theprint.in/world/nigeria-charges-protesters-with-treason-inciting-military/2249248/) | Reuters via ThePrint | 2024-09-02  
  Prosecutors framed protesters as destabilizers and mutineers. That is negative evidence for information freedom because it shows the state using criminal law to discourage challenge and shape public narratives.  
  Question IDs: `4B.6`, also `4B.2`, `4B.3`, `4B.5`

- [Nigeria charges 76 including minors with treason after August protests](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/nigeria-charges-76-including-minors-with-treason-after-august-protests-3698000) | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-11-01  
  Reuters reported that the case expanded to 76 defendants, including minors, after the protests. This strengthens the negative reading that the state treated dissent as a security threat rather than protecting open public information flows.  
  Question IDs: `4B.6`, also `4B.2`, `4B.3`, `4B.5`

- [Nigeria considers tough penalties for subversive acts under proposed law](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/nigeria-considers-tough-penalties-for-subversive-acts-under-proposed-law-3571782) | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-08-14  
  Reuters reported a proposed Counter Subversion Bill criticized as a crackdown on dissent after the protests. The proposal itself is negative evidence for media and information freedom, even though it was later withdrawn.  
  Question IDs: `4B.6`, also `4B.3`, `4B.5`

**Search gap**
- I found **no strong direct 2024 evidence** that Tinubu created new protections for independent media, broadcast autonomy, or public information access.
- I also found **no clear evidence** of a press-freedom reform package strong enough to offset the Cybercrimes Act and journalist prosecutions.
- The best-supported reading is therefore **negative overall**, with only **general democratic rhetoric** on the positive side.
